lessons.title: Life Is a Warfare
lessons.imageAlt: Hubert Robert — Equestrian Statue of Marcus Aurelius on the Capitoline (1757), full landscape drawing, Metropolitan Museum of Art
lessons.quote: Life is a warfare and a stranger's sojourn, and after-fame is oblivion.
lessons.lesson: Armor and appearance are not the thing. Marcus wrote as emperor on campaign: body a stream, soul a vapor, fame a fog. The campaign is the life. Trials forge the warrior because the field does not pause for reputation. Strategy over raw strength is philosophy—one governing mind that holds when the sojourn turns hard. After-fame is oblivion; the work is the watch you keep today.
lessons.today: Treat one inconvenience as the campaign, not an insult. Hold the post. Do the next necessary thing without asking who will remember it.

lessons.title: I Will Endure It
lessons.imageAlt: Arnold Böcklin — Odysseus and Polyphemus (1896), full landscape painting of Odysseus at sea after the trial of the cave
lessons.source: Homer, Odyssey Book 5 (A. T. Murray translation)
lessons.quote: And if again some god shall smite me on the wine-dark sea, I will endure it, having in my breast a heart that endureth affliction.
lessons.lesson: Calypso offered Odysseus immortality on a soft island. He chose the raft. Armor and appearance are not the thing—neither is a goddess's bed. Trials forge the warrior who will take the wine-dark sea rather than a life that costs him his name. Strategy over raw strength: he does not deny the wreck that may come; he budgets for it in the heart before he leaves the shore. Faith under pressure is the decision to go home when staying would be easier.
lessons.today: Refuse one soft berth that would keep you from the work that is actually yours. Build the raft. Put to sea.
